operations.name: join
operations.description:
Register a new user account in the Todo List application.

This endpoint creates a new user record in the todo_list_users table with the provided email and password. The email must be unique across all users in the system and will be used as the primary identifier for future authentication. The password will be securely hashed using industry-standard bcrypt algorithm with appropriate salt before being stored.

The system performs validation on the email format to ensure it conforms to standard email specifications. Password strength requirements are enforced at the application level to ensure security. Upon successful registration, the user will receive initial JWT tokens for authentication.

This is a public endpoint that does not require prior authentication, allowing new users to create accounts. The operation will fail if the email is already registered or if the provided credentials do not meet system requirements.

After successful registration, users can proceed to login using the /auth/user/login endpoint to obtain access tokens for managing their todo items.

requestBody.description: User registration information including email and password

responseBody.description: Authorized user information with access tokens

operations.name: login
operations.description:
Authenticate a user and generate access tokens.

This endpoint validates user credentials against the stored information in the todo_list_users table. The email and password are checked for correctness, with the password being securely compared against the bcrypt hashed value stored in the database.

Upon successful authentication, the system generates a new JWT access token and refresh token for the user. A session record is also created in the todo_list_user_sessions table to track this authentication event, storing connection context information such as IP address and referrer for security monitoring purposes.

This is a public endpoint that allows users to obtain access tokens without prior authentication. The operation will fail if the email does not exist or if the password is incorrect.

After successful login, users can use their access tokens to authenticate requests to protected endpoints for managing their todo items. The refresh token can be used with the /auth/user/refresh endpoint to obtain new access tokens when they expire.

responseBody.description: Authorized user information with access tokens

operations.name: refresh
operations.description:
Refresh an expired access token using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint allows authenticated users to obtain a new access token when their current one expires. The provided refresh token is validated against the system's token store to ensure it is still valid and has not been revoked or expired.

The refresh token mechanism provides seamless user experience by allowing continued access to the application without requiring users to re-enter their credentials frequently. The system maintains security by tracking refresh token usage and can invalidate tokens if suspicious activity is detected.

This endpoint requires a valid refresh token in the Authorization header, indicating that the user has previously authenticated. The operation will fail if the refresh token is invalid, expired, or has been revoked.

After successful token refresh, users receive new access tokens that can be used to authenticate requests to protected endpoints for managing their todo items. This enables uninterrupted usage of the application while maintaining security.

responseBody.description: Authorized user information with refreshed access tokens

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of todo items from the system. This operation operates on the todo_list_todos table from the Prisma schema and provides advanced search capabilities for finding todos based on multiple criteria including partial title matching, completion status filtering, creation date ranges, and user ownership.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Todos can be sorted by creation date, last update, title, or completion status in ascending or descending order.

Security considerations include proper user context filtering to ensure users can only access their own todo items. The system automatically filters results based on the authenticated user's identity, preventing unauthorized access to other users' data.

This operation integrates with the todo_list_todos table as defined in the Prisma schema, incorporating all available todo fields and relationships. The response includes todo summary information optimized for list displays, with options to include additional details based on authorization level.

The newly created todo item will be associated with the authenticated user who made the request.

The operation validates that the title is provided and not empty, ensuring that every todo item has a meaningful description of the task to be completed. Maximum length constraints are enforced to maintain data quality and prevent abuse. The system automatically populates metadata fields including creation and modification timestamps.

This operation integrates with the todo_list_todos table as defined in the Prisma schema, which enforces a foreign key relationship to the authenticated user. IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

A page.

email.description:
Unique email address used for user authentication.

Must be a valid email format and is case-insensitive for login purposes. This field serves as the primary identifier for user authentication and must be unique across all user accounts in the system. The email validation ensures only properly formatted email addresses are accepted.

This corresponds to the email field in the todo_list_users Prisma model which is defined with a unique constraint to prevent duplicate registrations. The case-insensitive handling ensures consistent user experience regardless of input case during login attempts.

password.description:
Securely hashed password for user authentication.

This password will be securely hashed using industry-standard bcrypt algorithm with appropriate salt before storage. It must meet system requirements for strength and complexity to ensure account security. The plain text password is only used during registration and is never stored in plain text form.

The password handling follows security best practices with proper hashing algorithms and salting techniques. The bcrypt implementation includes appropriate cost factors to balance security with performance considerations.

ITodoListUserListUser.IJoin.description:
Request to register a new user account in the Todo List application.

This data structure is used when creating a new user account through the registration process. It contains the essential information needed to establish a user's identity in the system, including their email address and password. The registration also captures connection context information for security monitoring purposes.

Upon successful registration, the user will receive initial JWT tokens for authentication. The email must be unique across all users in the system, and the password will be securely hashed before storage.

Note that while the ip field is optional (as the server can extract the IP from the request), both href and referrer are mandatory as they provide crucial context that the server cannot infer. These session context fields are required for creating a proper authentication session record even for the initial registration.

The data structure follows security best practices with secure password handling and comprehensive session tracking to detect and prevent fraudulent registration attempts.

email.description: User's email address used for authentication. Must be a valid email format.

password.description: User's password for authentication. This should be the plain text password that will be securely hashed by the backend for storage and comparison.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking. This is optional as the server can extract the IP from the request, but the client may provide it for server-side rendering scenarios.

href.description: Connection URL representing the current page the user is on when logging in. This provides context about where the login request originated.

referrer.description: Referrer URL representing the previous page the user was on before arriving at the login page. This helps track user navigation patterns for security monitoring.

ITodoListUserListUser.ILogin.description:
User login credentials for authentication.

This DTO contains the necessary information for a user to authenticate with the system. The email and password are used to verify the user's identity against the stored credentials in the todo_list_users table.

The email field must be a valid email address format that matches the user's registered email. The password should be the plain text version which will be securely compared against the bcrypt hashed value stored in the database.

In addition to authentication credentials, this DTO includes session context fields that provide connection metadata for security monitoring purposes. The href and referrer fields are mandatory for tracking user navigation patterns, while the IP address is optional since the server can extract it from the request.

These session context fields are stored in the todo_list_user_sessions table to maintain an audit trail of authentication events, enabling security monitoring and potential fraud detection.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated user.

This UUID corresponds to the primary key of the authenticated user in the todo_list_users table. It uniquely identifies the user account within the system and matches the id property in the ITodoListUser entity. This allows clients to identify which user account the authorization tokens are associated with.

email.description:
Unique email address used for user authentication. Must be a valid email format and is case-insensitive for login purposes.

This field serves as the primary identifier for user authentication. It must be unique across all user accounts in the system. The email validation ensures only properly formatted email addresses are accepted. The system treats email addresses as case-insensitive for login purposes to improve user experience.

ITodoListUserListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Response with authorized user information and access tokens.

This data structure is returned upon successful user authentication (login) or token refresh operations. It contains the essential information needed for a client to maintain an authenticated session with the Todo List application, including the user's identifier and the necessary authentication tokens.

The id field provides the unique identifier for the authenticated user, which matches their record in the todo_list_users table. The token field contains the JWT tokens required for authenticating subsequent requests to protected API endpoints. This structure enables seamless access to the application's features while maintaining security through token-based authentication.

page.description: Page number for pagination. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. Used in conjunction with limit to retrieve specific subsets of todo items.

limit.description: Number of todos to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100. Controls the page size for pagination to prevent excessive data transfer.

ITodoListUserTodo.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for retrieving todo items with pagination.

This DTO defines the query parameters available for retrieving todo items with basic pagination. It allows users to retrieve specific pages of their todo list with a configurable page size.

Pagination is implemented through the page and limit parameters, allowing efficient retrieval of todo lists without overwhelming the client or network.

All fields are optional, allowing retrieval of the first page with default sizing when no parameters are provided.

id.description:
Primary Key.

Unique identifier for the todo item. This is the primary key for the todo_list_todos table in the database. It follows the UUID format to ensure global uniqueness across the system. This identifier is automatically generated when a new todo item is created and is used for all subsequent operations on the item, including retrieval, updates, and deletion.

The UUID format provides several advantages:
- Guaranteed uniqueness without requiring coordination
- Security through obscurity (harder to guess than sequential IDs)
- Distributed system compatibility
- Database independence

This field is immutable once set and will never change throughout the lifecycle of the todo item.

todo_list_user_id.description:
The user who owns this todo item. {@link todo_list_users.id}.

This field establishes the ownership relationship between the todo item and the user who created it. Every todo item must be associated with exactly one user account in the system. This foreign key constraint ensures data integrity by preventing orphaned todo items and enables efficient querying of user-specific todo lists.

The relationship is mandatory - every todo item must have an owner. The system automatically sets this field based on the authenticated user context when a new todo item is created. Users can only access and modify todo items that belong to their own account, which is enforced through this field.

This field is indexed in the database to support efficient lookups of todos by user. Combined with other fields like creation time and completion status, it enables performant retrieval of user-specific todo collections.

title.description:
The descriptive text of the task to be completed. This field contains the main content of the todo item that describes what needs to be done. Maximum length is 255 characters to ensure concise task descriptions.

This field is required for all todo items and can be modified by the user at any time through update operations. The system performs validation to ensure the title meets length requirements and is not empty.

Business rules:
- Must not be empty or contain only whitespace
- Maximum length of 255 characters
- Should clearly describe a single actionable task
- Cannot be null (not nullable in database)

description.description:
Optional detailed description providing additional context or information about the task. This field allows users to add more comprehensive information beyond the title. Maximum length is 1000 characters.

This field is optional and can be modified by the user at any time through update operations. The system performs validation to ensure the description meets length requirements when provided.

Business rules:
- Optional field (nullable in database)
- Maximum length of 1000 characters when provided

completed.description:
Status indicator showing whether the task has been completed. True indicates the task is completed, false indicates it is still pending. This field supports the core functionality of the todo application.

Users can toggle this status at any time through update operations. The field has appropriate indexes in the database to support efficient querying of completed vs pending items.

Business rules:
- Required field (cannot be null)
- Default value is false (new items are pending)
- Can be changed at any time by the user
- Indexed in database for efficient filtering

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was initially created. This field provides an audit trail of when tasks were added to the system and supports ordering of tasks by creation time.

This field is immutable once set and will never change throughout the lifecycle of the todo item. It provides important context for users to understand when they created a task and can be used for sorting and filtering operations.

Business rules:
- Automatically set by system on creation
- Cannot be modified by user
- Uses ISO 8601 date-time format
- Indexed in database for efficient querying
- Never null

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was last modified. This field automatically updates whenever any changes are made to the task, providing an audit trail of modifications.

This field provides important context for users to understand when they last updated a task. It can be used for sorting and filtering operations based on modification time.

Business rules:
- Automatically updated by system on any modification
- Uses ISO 8601 date-time format
- Never null

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the todo item was soft deleted. NULL indicates an active item. This field is essential for content recovery and maintaining audit trails while allowing content management.

This field enables soft deletion functionality, where items are marked as deleted without being permanently removed from the database. This approach supports:
- Content recovery in case of accidental deletion
- Audit trails for compliance purposes
- Data integrity by maintaining references
- Efficient cleanup operations

When this field is NULL, the item is considered active. When populated with a timestamp, the item is considered deleted and typically excluded from normal queries unless explicitly requested. Applications should filter out items with non-NULL deleted_at values in standard list views.

ITodoListUserTodo.description:
Todo items created by authenticated users.

This table stores individual task items that users create to track their personal activities and responsibilities. Each todo item is associated with exactly one user who owns and manages it. The table maintains both the current state of the task and timestamps for audit purposes.

Todos can be in either a pending or completed state, which is tracked in the completed field. Users can update task details including the title and completion status at any time. The system automatically maintains creation and modification timestamps.

The relationship to users is strictly enforced with a foreign key constraint ensuring data integrity. Each todo item can only belong to one user, and users can have multiple todo items.

For performance optimization, the table includes appropriate indexes to support common query patterns such as retrieving a user's todo items and filtering by completion status. Soft deletion is supported through the deleted_at field to maintain audit trails while allowing content management.

title.description:
The descriptive text of the task to be completed.

This field contains the main content of the todo item that describes what needs to be done. It must be a non-empty string with a maximum length of 255 characters to ensure concise task descriptions. The title should clearly communicate the action or task that needs to be completed.

In the creation context, this field is required as it provides the essential identifying information for the new todo item. Users must provide a meaningful title when creating tasks to ensure they can distinguish between different items in their todo list.

ITodoListUserTodo.ICreate.description:
Creation parameters for new todo items in the system.

This data transfer object defines the required and optional fields that users must provide when creating new todo items in their personal task list. The schema represents a minimal but complete set of information needed to initialize a new task with all essential attributes.

The creation process requires a title as the minimum identifying information for the task. Users may optionally provide a more detailed description to add context to the task. The system automatically populates all other fields including:
- Unique identifier (ID)
- Creation timestamp
- Last update timestamp (initially same as creation)
- Completion status (defaults to false)
- User association (from authentication context)
- Soft deletion flag (initially null)

This DTO directly corresponds to the 'todo_list_todos' table in the database schema, specifically mapping to user-provided fields. All system-managed fields are automatically handled by the backend service during the creation process.

title.description:
The descriptive text of the task to be completed.

This field contains the main content of the todo item that describes what needs to be done. Users can modify this field to update the primary task description. It must be a non-empty string with a maximum length of 255 characters to ensure concise task descriptions.

In the update context, this field is optional and can be omitted if the user doesn't want to change the title. When provided, the system performs validation to ensure the title meets length requirements and is not empty.

completed.description:
Status indicator showing whether the task has been completed.

This field represents the current status of the todo item. A value of true indicates the task is completed, while false indicates it is still pending. Users can toggle this status at any time through update operations to track their progress.

In the update context, this field is optional and can be omitted if the user doesn't want to change the completion status. When provided, the value must be a valid boolean.

ITodoListUserTodo.IUpdate.description:

This data transfer object defines the fields that can be modified for an existing todo item. It supports partial updates, meaning users can modify just the title, just the description, just the completion status, or any combination of these fields. Fields not included in the update request will retain their current values.

All fields are optional in this DTO to support partial updates, but the system performs validation on provided fields to ensure data quality. The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed whenever any field is modified.

This DTO directly corresponds to the 'todo_list_todos' table in the database schema, specifically mapping to the fields that users are allowed to modify. System-managed fields like ID, creation timestamp, and user association cannot be modified through this interface for security and data integrity reasons.

ITodoListUserTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of todo items for list views and search results.

This DTO provides a lightweight representation of todo items optimized for list views and search results. It includes essential information needed to display todo items in a list format while excluding verbose fields like soft deletion timestamps.

The summary format is designed for efficient API responses when retrieving multiple todo items. It excludes optional fields like deleted_at to reduce payload size while maintaining all critical information for users to identify and understand their tasks.

This DTO is typically used in paginated responses and list operations where including full details for every item would be unnecessarily verbose. Users can retrieve full details for specific items using the main ITodoListTodo DTO through individual item retrieval operations.
